raw_response:
I am old now, and I do not like taking big risks. Our land is only 16.1 mu, so I still do what has worked on our fields. Wheat and maize together keep the land busy and keep income steadier. Last year, if the crop looked weak, adding a bit more fertilizer helped, so I will not cut too much. But money is still money, and some people in the house work outside, so I cannot count on everyone being free at the busy time. For wheat, I will sow in early October like everyone here, use a common improved variety I can get nearby, put most fertilizer at sowing, then topdress once when the wheat starts growing strongly in spring. If the winter and spring stay dry, I will irrigate a few times from the well, but not too many because pumping costs money. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize right away. That gap is very short, so I will keep land preparation simple and fast. Maize usually follows the wheat stubble quickly here. I will use hybrid seed, give enough fertilizer so the stand does not turn yellow, and irrigate only if rain is short, because summer rain sometimes saves that cost. I do not spray unless I see a real problem, but I usually use herbicide to save labor.
